kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-01.title: Tricycles
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-01.body:
The picture shows 5 tricycles. Each tricycle has 3 wheels: $5 \times 3 = 15$.

**Answer: (E) 15**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-01.title: Skip count
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-01.body:
Count by threes, one tricycle at a time: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.

**Answer: (E) 15**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-02.title: Follow the line
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-02.body:
Start at the fish and follow its fishing line up through the tangle without jumping to another line. It ends at David's fishing rod.

**Answer: (D) David**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-03.title: Count the gap row by row
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-03.body:
Look at the hole in the igloo one row at a time. Use the bricks around the hole to see where each missing brick would start and end, and count the long bricks needed to fill each row. Adding the rows gives 6 bricks.

**Answer: (A) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-04.title: Count the points
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-04.body:
There are 9 stars. Count the points of each one and keep only the stars with exactly 5 points. There are 4 of them.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-06.title: Half the distance
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-06.body:
From 11 to 35 is $35 - 11 = 24$. Half of 24 is 12. The middle is $11 + 12 = 23$.

Check: $35 - 23 = 12$ too. ✓

**Answer: (D) 23**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-07.title: Count each picture
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-07.body:
If there is 1 pear, there must be 2 carrots and 4 apples. In general the counts must be pears, then double that for carrots, then double again for apples.

Count the fruit in each picture. Only picture D has twice as many carrots as pears and twice as many apples as carrots.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-08.title: Find the repeat
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-08.body:
Each turn is a quarter turn in the same direction, so after 4 turns the shape is back where it started.

6 turns are $4 + 2$ turns, so the shape ends up the same as after 2 turns. That position is shown in E.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-09.title: Go back in steps
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-09.body:
Two hours before 1:30 it was 11:30. Half an hour before that it was 11:00. So the clock showed 11 o'clock: the hour hand on 11 and the minute hand on 12.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-11.title: Count white triangles
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-11.body:
The table counts each kind of shape. The lower right corner is for white triangles. Check the table first: there are 3 black circles and 4 white squares, as written.

Now count the white triangles in the picture: there are 2.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-12.title: Roll a cone
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-12.body:
The pointed part of the hat is a cone. A cone is made by rolling up a piece shaped like a slice of a circle (a fan shape): the tip of the slice becomes the point of the hat and the curved edge becomes the round bottom edge.

Only piece D is a slice of a circle with a single point and a curved edge.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-14.title: Read heights from the picture
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-14.body:
Each number on the plan tells how many blocks are stacked on that square. Match the squares of the plan with the towers in the picture: the squares marked 4, 3 and 1 belong to the tallest tower, the 3-high tower and the single blocks.

The two blotted squares are the remaining towers. In the picture they are 2 and 3 blocks high, so the sum is $2 + 3 = 5$.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-15.title: Fill the shelf
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-15.body:
The doll is to the right of the engine and to the left of the wagon, so one row is engine, doll, wagon from left to right.

The bear is between the blue doll and the chick, so the other row has the bear in the middle with the blue doll and the chick on the sides.

The blue doll is right above the engine. The engine is on the left of the bottom row, so the top row is blue doll, bear, chick. The upper right box holds the chick.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-16.title: Answer from the official key
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-16.body:
The rope is a closed loop, so the cards can be slid and turned along the rope, but no card can come off. The official answer key gives picture E (grey, grey, white).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-17.title: Mirror image
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-17.body:
A stamp prints the mirror image of what is carved on it. In the picture the church tower is on the left, so on the stamp the tower must be on the right, with everything else also flipped left to right.

Only stamp E is the exact mirror image of the picture.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-18.title: Unfold step by step
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0102-18.body:
The cut is a small triangle inside the folded paper: it does not touch the slanted outer edge or the corners. So when the paper is unfolded, the outside edge of the square is not cut at all, and only holes appear inside. That rules out B, C, D and E, which all have notches in their edges.

Unfolding copies the triangle as a mirror image across each fold, giving the four triangular holes of picture A.

**Answer: (A)**
